Presents for follow-up after percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stent placement.

The patient, with hypertension and hyperlipidemia managed since 2020 and 2021 and frontotemporal dementia diagnosed in 2023, returns for follow-up after undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention with placement of a drug-eluting stent (DES) in the left anterior descending artery 3 months ago. The procedure was performed after exertional angina and significant luminal narrowing on coronary angiography.
The cardiologist explains that the drug coating helps reduce the risk of in-stent restenosis, which was more common with older bare-metal stents.

Recurrent episodes of substernal chest discomfort occurring at rest and waking him from sleep.

The patient is a 62-year-old male with coronary artery disease status post percutaneous coronary intervention in 2025, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and frontotemporal dementia who presents with recurrent chest discomfort. He describes the pain as tight and pressure-like, occurring primarily at rest and sometimes waking him from sleep.
